title: Digital Electronics

notes.heading: 1. Radix Conversions, 2's Complement & Boolean / De Morgan Laws
notes.proseLatex: An $n$-bit unsigned binary word spans $0$ to $2^n - 1$, whereas $n$-bit $2$'s complement signed integers span $-2^{n-1}$ to $+(2^{n-1} - 1)$ (e.g., $-128$ to $+127$ for $8$ bits; $2$'s complement $= 1$'s complement $+ 1$). Core Boolean simplifications: Absorption $A + AB = A$ and $A + \bar{A}B = A + B$; Distributive $A + BC = (A+B)(A+C)$; Consensus $AB + \bar{A}C + BC = AB + \bar{A}C$; and De Morgan's theorems $\overline{A\cdot B} = \bar{A} + \bar{B}$ and $\overline{A + B} = \bar{A}\cdot\bar{B}$ ('break the line, change the sign'!).

keyFormulas.label: De Morgan's Laws, Absorption & Consensus Identities
keyFormulas.latex: $\overline{AB} = \bar{A} + \bar{B},\quad \overline{A + B} = \bar{A}\bar{B},\quad A + \bar{A}B = A + B,\quad AB + \bar{A}C + BC = AB + \bar{A}C$
keyFormulas.aiExplainContext: Minimize Boolean SOP/POS expressions rapidly without full K-maps.

examples.problemLatex: Simplify the Boolean expression $Y = A\bar{B} + AB + \bar{A}B$.
stepsLatex: Group first two terms: $A(\bar{B} + B) + \bar{A}B = A\cdot 1 + \bar{A}B = A + \bar{A}B$.

notes.heading: 2. Logic Gates, XOR/XNOR Properties & Universal Gate Counts (NAND / NOR)
notes.proseLatex: XOR $A\oplus B = \bar{A}B + A\bar{B}$ acts as an odd-parity detector and controlled inverter ($A\oplus 0 = A$, $A\oplus 1 = \bar{A}$, $A\oplus A = 0$), while XNOR $A\odot B = AB + \bar{A}\bar{B}$ tests equality (for odd number of inputs, $A\oplus B\oplus C = A\odot B\odot C$!). NAND and NOR are UNIVERSAL gates; memorize the exact minimum $2$-input NAND / NOR realization table so you never waste exam minutes drawing gates!

keyFormulas.label: Minimum 2-Input NAND / NOR Gate Counts
keyFormulas.latex: $\text{Via NAND (NOT, AND, OR, XOR, XNOR)} = (1,\,2,\,3,\,4,\,5);\qquad \text{Via NOR} = (1,\,3,\,2,\,5,\,4)$
keyFormulas.aiExplainContext: Recall minimum 2-input NAND vs NOR counts for basic gates and half-adders (5 NANDs or 5 NORs).

notes.heading: 3. Adders, Multiplexers & Flip-Flop Counters
notes.proseLatex: A Half Adder adds $A, B$ to give $\text{Sum} = A\oplus B$ and $\text{Carry} = AB$; a Full Adder adds $A, B, C_{\text{in}}$ giving $\text{Sum} = A\oplus B\oplus C_{\text{in}}$ and $\text{Carry} = AB + BC_{\text{in}} + CA_{\text{in}}$. A $2^n:1$ Multiplexer (universal combinational block!) requires $n$ select lines. Sequential circuits add memory: JK flip-flop cures SR's invalid $S=R=1$ state by toggling ($Q^+ = \bar{Q}$ when $J=K=1$), T flip-flop divides clock frequency by $2$ per stage, and an $N$-bit ripple/MOD-$M$ counter ($M \le 2^N$) divides input clock frequency to $f_{\text{out}} = f_{\text{clk}}/M$.

keyFormulas.label: Full Adder Equations, MUX Select Lines & Counter Modulus
keyFormulas.latex: $S_{\text{FA}} = A\oplus B\oplus C_{\text{in}},\quad C_{\text{out}} = AB + BC_{\text{in}} + AC_{\text{in}},\quad N_{\text{FF}} = \lceil\log_2 M\rceil,\quad f_{\text{out}} = \frac{f_{\text{clk}}}{M}$
keyFormulas.aiExplainContext: Count flip-flops needed for MOD-M counters (e.g., 4 FFs for MOD-10 decade counter) and output frequency.

examples.problemLatex: A $16\text{ MHz}$ clock drives a cascade of a MOD-$10$ decade counter followed by $3$ T flip-flops (wired with $T = 1$). Find the final output frequency.
stepsLatex: Three T flip-flops divide by $2^3 = 8$; combined modulus $M = 10 \times 8 = 80$.

wbjeebTraps: Minimum NAND vs NOR swap trap: XOR needs $4$ NANDs (or $5$ NORs), whereas XNOR needs $5$ NANDs (or $4$ NORs)!
For $3$ variables, $A\oplus B\oplus C = A\odot B\odot C$ (ODD-input XOR and XNOR are identical; they remain complements ONLY for EVEN number of inputs!).
An $8$-bit $2$'s complement signed number spans $-128$ to $+127$, NOT $-127$ to $+128$.
